Bound struct slab readers to the source array size

Also right-size the fixed-rank index/stride bookkeeping arrays in
Mat_VarGetStructs to the enforced rank limit (9) instead of
over-allocating 10 elements.

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/pull/317
(cherry picked from commit 2d7c34e9bf5dd9db4e02874968ce35fffc1d3b52)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Validate edge product in Mat_VarGetCells and Mat_VarGetStructs

Now that the edge product is validated up front, also relax
Mat_VarGetStructs' rank check to allow the same maximum rank (10)
already supported by the other fixed-rank slab readers in mat5.c and
read_data.c.

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/pull/318

(cherry picked from commit d410ad4bd15efd286d3ee587b052847bf073c454)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: Mat_VarGetStructs (src/matvar_struct.c) uses three fixed-size stack arrays (idx, cnt, dimp) indexed 0..matvar->rank-1 to walk a struct array's dimensions. Commit 66c68c2 ('Bound struct slab readers to the source array size') right-sizes those arrays from 10 to 9 elements, which is exactly correct and benign on its own because the function's rank guard at that point in history is 'if (matvar->rank > 9) return NULL;' (rank 0..9 needs only indices 0..8, i.e. 9 slots). Commit 2bf5677 ('Validate edge product in Mat_VarGetCells and Mat_VarGetStructs'), read on its own, only adds an edge-product overflow guard (CheckEdgeOverflow) and relaxes the rank check from 'rank > 9' to 'rank > 10' -- by itself this looks like a reasonable cleanup that harmonizes Mat_VarGetStructs with the rank-10 limit already used by every other fixed-rank slab reader in the codebase (GetDataSlab in mat5.c, ReadDataSlabN/ReadDataSlab2 in read_data.c, and even Mat_VarGetStructsLinear in the same file use 'rank > 10'), and the edge overflow check it adds has nothing to do with array sizing. Neither diff is wrong when read against its own immediate parent: 66c68c2's arrays exactly match the rank cap that exists at that point in history, and 2bf5677 never touches the array declarations at all. Only when both edits are composed does rank=10 become reachable while idx/cnt/dimp hold just 9 elements, so the loop 'for (j = 1; j < matvar->rank; j++)' writes idx[9]/dimp[9] one element past the end of each stack array. A correct fix must look at both commits together: restoring either the array size (back to 10) or the rank cap (back to 9) alone removes the overflow, but a reviewer examining only 2bf5677's diff has no way to see that the rank limit it relaxes is exactly the limit another, earlier commit depended on when it chose the new array size.
